SEC regular season champions |tourney= [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result = Final Four }} {{2014–15 Southeastern Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2014–15 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Kentucky]] in the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2014–15 college basketball season]]. The team played its home games in [[Lexington, Kentucky]], United States for the 39th consecutive season at [[Rupp Arena]], with a capacity of 23,500. The team was led by sixth-year head coach [[John Calipari]]. The team was a National semifinalist in the [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], competed in the school's 17th Final Four. It was Calipari's fourth Final Four appearance at Kentucky. The team finished the regular season with a perfect 31–0 record, the best start in school history. For six years, they had been the last unbeaten team to enter the NCAA tournament until [[2020-21 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]] in 2021.{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/02/17/kentucky-wildcats-tennessee-best-start-school-history|title=Kentucky off to best start in school history after win over Tennessee|access-date=2015-02-17|date=2015-04-06|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} Their 38 wins is tied with the [[2011–12 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2012 Kentucky team]] for the most in men's Division I history.{{cite web|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2015/04/05/short-perfection-kentucky-basketball-team-remembered-now/25333799/|title=How should the 38-1 Wildcats be remembered?|access-date=2015-04-05|date=2015-04-06|work=[[Courier-Journal]]|author=Tucker, Kyle}} Their 38–1 record (.974 winning percentage) is the best by a team that did not finish undefeated. After finishing as the National Runner-up in the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2014 NCAA tournament]], the expectations for this team were high. The team, however, would be without some of its top players from the [[2013–14 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2013–14 team]] including starting power forward [[Julius Randle]]{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2014/04/22/kentuckys-julius-randle-declares-for-the-nba-draft/8005193/|title=Kentucky's Julius Randle declares for the NBA draft|access-date=2015-03-25|date=2014-04-22|work=[[USA Today]]|author=Tucker, Kyle}}{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/nba/point-forward/2014/04/22/julius-randle-declares-draft-kentucky|title=Kentucky's Julius Randle declares for the NBA draft|access-date=2015-03-25|date=2014-04-22|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|author=Golliver, Ben}} and starting small forward [[James Young (basketball)|James Young]],{{cite web|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2014/04/17/kentuckys-james-young-declares-nba-draft/7831807/|title=Kentucky's James Young declares for NBA draft|access-date=2015-03-25|date=2014-04-17|work=[[Courier-Journal]]|author=Tucker, Kyle}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2014/story/_/id/10797286/james-young-kentucky-wildcats-declares-nba-draft|title=James Young declares for draft|access-date=2015-03-25|date=2014-04-18|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Goodman, Jeff}} who were first-round draft choices in the [[2014 NBA draft]]. John Calipari announced four players for his 2014 class during the early signing period on November 14. [[Trey Lyles]] (Indianapolis), [[Karl-Anthony Towns]] (Metuchen, N.J.), [[Devin Booker]] (Grand Rapids, Mich.) and [[Tyler Ulis]] (Chicago Heights, Ill.) all signed national letters of intent to play basketball at the University of Kentucky, starting in the 2014–15 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/blog/2013/11/never-count-john-calipari-out.html|title=UK, Calipari sign four for 2014|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2013-11-14|publisher=University of Kentucky|archive-date=April 2, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402132117/http://www.ukathletics.com/blog/2013/11/never-count-john-calipari-out.html|url-status=dead}} Karl-Anthony Towns was the first commitment for the class when he verbally committed on December 4, 2012.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/8708701/karl-towns-jr-gives-oral-commitment-kentucky-reclassified-junior|title=Karl Towns Jr. commits to Kentucky|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2012-12-04|publisher=ESPN}} He was named [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade National Player of the Year]] in 2014.{{cite web|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2014/07/16/kentucky-basketballs-karl-anthony-towns-wins-gatorade-player-year/12727841/|title=UK's Towns named Gatorade Athlete of the Year|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2014-07-16|publisher=Courier-Journal}} He played for the Dominican Republic National Team in 2012 and 2013 which were coached by John Calipari and Kentucky assistant, [[Orlando Antigua]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/high-school/boys-basketball/story/_/id/8001784/new-jersey-native-karl-towns-jr-16-play-dominican-republic-olympic-qualifying|title=Towns Jr. going global|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2012-06-18|publisher=ESPN}} He was ranked as No. 6 overall by ESPN and No. 11 by Rivals and Scout. Tyler Ulis was the second commitment in the class when he verbally committed on September 13, 2013.{{cite web|url=http://www.kentucky.com/2013/09/13/2820594/chicago-point-guard-ulis-commits.html|title=Chicago point guard Ulis commits to Kentucky|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2013-09-13|publisher=Lexington Herald-Leader|author=Roberts, Ben}} He committed to Kentucky briefly after he was offered a scholarship. Kentucky had just missed on their primary target, [[Emmanuel Mudiay]], when he committed to [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]] on August 24, 2013.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/story/_/id/9597797/emmanuel-mudiay-no-2-point-guard-commits-smu-mustangs|title=Emmanuel Mudiay commits to SMU|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2013-08-24|publisher=ESPN}} Ulis, however, quickly rose in the recruiting rankings, finishing No. 20 overall by Scout, No. 21 overall by Rivals, and No. 25 overall by ESPN. He chose Kentucky over [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]], [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], and [[USC Trojans men's basketball|Southern Cal]]. Devin Booker was the third commitment in the class when he verbally committed on October 31, 2013.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/9908976/devin-booker-no-18-overall-prospect-commits-kentucky-wildcats|title=Devin Booker commits to Kentucky|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2013-10-31|publisher=ESPN}} He was ranked as the No. 18 overall by ESPN and No. 29 overall by Scout and Rivals. As a junior, he was named by Gatorade as the top basketball player in Mississippi.{{cite web|url=http://www.gatorade.com/poy/assets/writable/14581/2012-13_BK_DBooker.pdf|title=Devin Booker named Player of the Year|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2013-03-08|publisher=Gatorade}} He is the son of the former [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]] and All-American great [[Melvin Booker]]. He chose Kentucky over his Dad's alma mater and Michigan. This was Kentucky's seventh victory in eight games against Louisville with Calipari as head coach.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/122714aaa.html|title=Cats Outlast Cards for 58-50 Victory|access-date=2015-06-20|date=2014-12-27|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150621015108/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/122714aaa.html|archive-date=2015-06-21|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400587874|title=Kentucky vs Louisville boxscore|access-date=2015-06-20|date=2014-12-27|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} ===January=== Kentucky opened the SEC portion of their schedule on January 6 at home against [[2014–15 Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball team|Ole Miss]]. After looking dominant in November and December, the Cats were taken to the wire by the Rebels. UK needed overtime to outlast Ole Miss 89–86. Unfazed by trailing Kentucky 12 to 0 and 18 to 5, Ole Miss' Stefan Moody helped the Rebels regroup to mount runs of 10–0 and 7–0 to get within 23–22 before eventually taking a four-point lead with 7:01 left in the half. The Rebels led 38–36 at the break behind 50 percent shooting before Kentucky opened the second half with a spurt that put them by as many as six before Mississippi battled back. Wildcats guard Aaron Harrison thwarted the Rebels' quest by scoring 26 points, including two big free throws with 1:29 remaining in overtime to put Kentucky ahead to stay.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/010615aaa.html|title=Kentucky Edges Ole Miss 89-86 in Overtime|access-date=2015-01-06|date=2015-01-06|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150110010805/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/010615aaa.html|archive-date=2015-01-10|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400597317|title=Ole Miss vs Kentucky boxscore|access-date=2015-01-06|date=2015-01-06|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} After the scare Ole Miss put into Kentucky, they rebounded on January 10 at [[2014–15 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]] behind Booker's 18 points to a 70–64 victory in double-overtime. The Aggies rallied in the final minutes to tie it in regulation. Lyles made two foul shots with six seconds left in the first overtime for Kentucky, and Texas A&M took its time before missing a long 3 at the buzzer. Down 66 to 63, Texas A&M's Kourtney Roberson made one of two free throws before a turnover by Lyles gave the Aggies the ball back with 26.9 seconds left. Five combined 3-pointers by Vanderbilt's Riley LaChance (16 points) and Matthew Fisher-Davis (13) helped Vanderbilt pull within 58–54 with 2:36 left. The Commodores never got closer as the Harrisons closed it out for the Wildcats.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/012015aaa.html|title=Aaron Harrison's Big Second Half Leads Kentucky to 65-57 Win Over Vanderbilt|access-date=2015-01-20|date=2015-01-20|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150123235629/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/012015aaa.html|archive-date=2015-01-23|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400597343|title=Vanderbilt vs Kentucky boxscore|access-date=2015-01-20|date=2015-01-20|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} On January 24 Kentucky traveled to [[Columbia, South Carolina|Columbia]] to defeat [[2014–15 South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball team|South Carolina]] 58–43. Booker scored seven points in Kentucky's 14 to 0 run that spanned both halves, closing the surge with a 3-pointer that put the Wildcats ahead 37–24 with 18:28 remaining.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/012415aaa.html|title=Kentucky Defense Stifles South Carolina for 58-43 Win|access-date=2015-01-24|date=2015-01-24|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150127005612/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/012415aaa.html|archive-date=2015-01-27|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400597347|title=Kentucky vs South Carolina boxscore|access-date=2015-01-24|date=2015-01-24|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} On January 29 the Wildcats again traveled to [[Columbia, Missouri|Columbia]], this time to defeat Missouri 69 to 53. Missouri's Keanau Post started it with a rim-rattling dunk a few minutes in, and a pair of dunks by Ryan Rosburg had the fans in Mizzou Arena on their feet. Another dunk by Jakeenan Gant late in the half allowed the Tigers to close within 32–25. The Wildcats struggled some more early in the second half, throwing up a series of ugly jumpers and missing a couple shots at the rim. Missouri struggled to take advantage, but did close within 38 to 32 on Clark's basket with 14:25 to go. Foul trouble began to set in, though, with Missouri's Namon Wright and Montaque Gill-Caesar each picking up their fourth with more than 15 minutes left in the game. Aaron knocked down a jumper, and after Andrew did the same, he proceeded to the foul line on the next four trips down the floor. Wright fouled out with 8:52 to go. Gill-Caesar joined him less than a minute later. And by the time the Wildcats had hit those free throws, their lead had swelled to 56–36.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/012915aaa.html|title=Harrisons Headline 69-53 Win at Missouri|access-date=2015-01-29|date=2015-01-29|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150201204713/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/012915aaa.html|archive-date=2015-02-01|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400597360|title=Kentucky vs Missouri boxscore|access-date=2015-01-29|date=2015-01-29|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} On January 30 Kentucky faced off against Alabama for the second time this season at Rupp Arena, defeating the Crimson Tide 70 to 55. Cauley-Stein snapped out of a mini-slump with 12 points and four rebounds, Booker added 11 points with three 3-pointers and Aaron Harrison had 10. Kentucky quickly rolled to a double-digit lead and positioned itself to blow out Alabama before settling for a 37–24 advantage at the break. Kentucky controlled the paint 28 to 14 while their bench dominated the Tide 31–8. Kentucky also committed just five turnovers while forcing Alabama into 13 mistakes that resulted in 20 points.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/013115aaa.html|title=Balanced Attack Lifts Kentucky Past Alabama 70-55|access-date=2015-01-31|date=2015-01-31|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150204032357/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/013115aaa.html|archive-date=2015-02-04|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400597367|title=Alabama vs Kentucky boxscore|access-date=2015-01-31|date=2015-01-31|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} ===February=== On February 3 Kentucky hosted [[2014–15 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|Georgia]] at Rupp Arena, defeating the Bulldogs 69 to 58. The Bulldogs were without leading scorer and rebounder Marcus Thornton, who was out due to a concussion. Andrew Harrison scored 23 points and combined with Towns for key baskets down the stretch that helped Kentucky pull away. Harrison's layup with 3:58 remaining provided a 62 to 54 lead before baskets by Georgia's [[Yante Maten]] and Nemanja Djurisic pulled the Bulldogs to 63 to 58 with 2:06 left. Towns' short jumper with 1:33 left got the lead to seven, and Tyler Ulis and Harrison each added two free throws in the final minute for the Wildcats.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/020315aaa.html|title=Towns, Andrew Harrison Spearhead 69-58 Win Over Georgia|access-date=2015-02-03|date=2015-02-03|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150207114030/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/020315aaa.html|archive-date=2015-02-07|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400597368|title=Georgia vs Kentucky boxscore|access-date=2015-02-03|date=2015-02-03|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} On February 7 Kentucky traveled to [[Gainesville, Florida|Gainesville]] to face arch-rival [[2014–15 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]]. Florida swept all three meetings in 2014, winning in Lexington, in Gainesville and in the [[2014 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]]. Both teams advanced to the Final Four in 2014, but had gone in different directions in 2015. Florida entered the game one game over .500 and struggling mightily through the beginning of SEC play. Aaron Harrison scored 23 points, Towns added 19 and the Wildcats remained unbeaten with a 68 to 61 victory over the Gators before a national television audience on ESPN's [[College GameDay (basketball)|College GameDay]]. Florida led by nine in the first half and used a 6 to 0 run to go up 44–42 midway through the second half. However, Cauley-Stein's dunk proved to be the turning point. Florida's Devon Robinson turned the ball over on one end, and Cauley-Stein was the beneficiary on the other. He caught a pass in transition near the foul line, took two steps and then slammed it over Robinson. He was fouled on the play and made the free throw to put Kentucky ahead for good. Free throws were huge down the stretch, too. Kentucky closed out the game from the charity stripe and finished 21 of 22 from there.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/020715aab.html|title=Cats Persevere, Defeat Florida 68-61 in Road Test|access-date=2015-02-07|date=2015-02-07|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210100901/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/020715aab.html|archive-date=2015-02-10|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400597381|title=Kentucky vs Florida boxscore|access-date=2015-02-07|date=2015-02-07|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} On February 9 traveled to [[Baton Rouge, Louisiana|Baton Rouge]] face [[2014–15 LSU Tigers basketball team|LSU]] before another national television audience on ESPN. Frustrated by the way his team was playing, coach Calipari told them he hoped they'd lose. They almost did. Towns redeemed himself after drawing a technical foul for hanging on the basket and the ire of his coach by hitting a go-head jump hook with 1:30 left and grabbing a clutch offensive rebound against LSU in the final minute to help Kentucky stay unbeaten, defeating the Tigers 71–69. Calipari explained that he wanted to make sure his team won't lose elimination games in March over senseless fouls, so even as his assistants pleaded with him to call timeout, he just watched and joined in the ear-ringing frenzy at the sold out Pete Maravich Assembly Center during a stunning 21–2 LSU run that gave the Tigers a 66 to 60 lead. LSU's Keith Hornsby had a shot to win it for LSU in the final seconds, but his off-balance 3 bounced off the outside of the rim, and Kentucky was victorious.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/021015aaa.html|title=Cauley-Stein, Towns Key in 71-69 Victory at LSU|access-date=2015-02-10|date=2015-02-10|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150211212239/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/021015aaa.html|archive-date=2015-02-11|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400597382|title=Kentucky vs LSU boxscore|access-date=2015-02-10|date=2015-02-10|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} On February 14 Kentucky returned to Rupp Arena to face off against South Carolina for the second time this season. Kentucky had a strong start that put South Carolina in a hole that steadily deepened. The Wildcats led 26 to 6 with 8:21 left in the first half and never eased off in overwhelming South Carolina on both ends. It was 43 to 18 at halftime, and Kentucky poured it on against a Gamecocks squad looking to build off a five-point win over Missouri.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/021415aaa.html|title=Kentucky Smothers South Carolina for 77-43 Win|access-date=2015-02-14|date=2015-02-14|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150216134022/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/021415aaa.html|archive-date=2015-02-16|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400597390|title=South Carolina vs Kentucky boxscore|access-date=2015-02-14|date=2015-02-14|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} On February 17 Kentucky traveled to [[Knoxville, Tennessee|Knoxville]] to face arch-rival [[2014–15 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]]. The victory set a new record for the historic program as they became 26–0 for the first time, though the Wildcats finished the 1953–54 season with a 25–0 mark.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/021715aaa.html|title=Kentucky Pulls Away from Tennessee for 66-48 Win|access-date=2015-02-17|date=2015-02-17|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221015619/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/021715aaa.html|archive-date=2015-02-21|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400597396|title=Kentucky vs Tennessee boxscore|access-date=2015-02-17|date=2015-02-17|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} On February 21 Kentucky returned to Rupp Arena to defeat [[2014–15 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]] 110 to 75. The victory also extended their best start ever and equaled the 1995–96 squad's school-record 27-game winning streak. At halftime Kentucky hoisted legendary player [[Tony Delk]]'s #00 jersey in the rafters.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/022115aaa.html|title=Towns Sparks Offensive Eruption in 110-75 Win|access-date=2015-02-21|date=2015-02-21|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150224085522/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/022115aaa.html|archive-date=2015-02-24|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400597407|title=Auburn vs Kentucky boxscore|access-date=2015-02-21|date=2015-02-21|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} On February 25 Kentucky traveled to [[Starkville, Mississippi|Starkville]] to face [[2014–15 Mississippi State Bulldogs basketball team|Mississippi State]]. Kentucky looked slightly mortal for most of the first half, letting a 14-point lead evaporate to 33 to 27. Ulis hit a 3-pointer just before the halftime buzzer to push the Wildcats' advantage to 36 to 27. They had a few more careless defensive moments early in the second half, which helped Mississippi State briefly make things interesting. Mississippi State's Craig Sword's pass to a wide-open Roquez Johnson led to an easy layup, pulling the Bulldogs within four with 15 minutes remaining. Kentucky responded with the next six points by pounding the ball into the paint and using its significant size advantage to pull away for the win. Lyles scored 18 points, and Kentucky was victorious 74–56.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/022515aaa.html|title=Lyles, Towns Lead Kentucky to 74-56 Win at Mississippi State|access-date=2015-02-25|date=2015-02-25|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228184529/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/022515aaa.html|archive-date=2015-02-28|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400597414|title=Kentucky vs Mississippi State boxscore|access-date=2015-02-25|date=2015-02-25|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} On February 28 Kentucky returned to Rupp Arena to face off against nationally ranked [[2014–15 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]]. The Razorbacks entered the game ranked No. 16/18 in the AP and USA Today Coaches polls. This was the first ranked opponent since they defeated Louisville in late December. Arkansas also entered the game on a three-game win streak over Kentucky. The Wildcats seized the tempo from the start with a quick pace that knocked the Razorbacks on their heels. Lyles started things off with a lob dunk from Towns (eight points, five rebounds), who followed with a putback basket. Arkansas went 0 for 9 from long range and shot 30 percent overall while getting outrebounded 24 to 18 through 20 minutes as Kentucky built a 42–26 halftime lead. At one point in the second half the lead swelled to 31 points. The Wildcats clinched the Southeastern Conference regular-season title defeating the Razorbacks 84–67.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/022815aaa.html|title=Kentucky Downs No. 16/18 Arkansas, Claims 46th SEC Title Outright|access-date=2015-02-28|date=2015-02-28|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150303151629/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/022815aaa.html|archive-date=2015-03-03|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400597420|title=Arkansas vs Kentucky boxscore|access-date=2015-02-28|date=2015-02-28|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} ===March=== On March 2 Kentucky traveled to [[Athens, Georgia|Athens]] to for its second meeting with Georgia. Facing the largest second-half deficit of its so-far perfect season, Kentucky clamped down defensively, ripped off a 14 to 0 run and defeat Georgia 72–64. Georgia's Yante Maten tipped in a miss of his own shot on the second attempt to put the Bulldogs up 56–47 with just over 9 minutes remaining. Towns and Aaron Harrison were huge down the stretch, combining for 12 of the 14 points during the decisive run. Towns had seven, including a three-point play with 2:53 left that put Kentucky ahead to stay. Harrison chipped in with five, and Cauley-Stein came up with a huge dunk off a missed free throw to give the Wildcats a four-point play on one possession.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030315aaa.html|title=Towns Powers Late Rally to Edge Georgia 72-64|access-date=2015-03-02|date=2015-03-02|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150306193852/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030315aaa.html|archive-date=2015-03-06|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400597425|title=Kentucky vs Georgia boxscore|access-date=2015-03-02|date=2015-03-02|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} On March 7, Kentucky returned to Rupp Arena to face Florida on senior night in the regular season finale. Kentucky embraced its milestone following the 67–50 victory over the Gators. The Wildcats gathered at midcourt and donned their blue T-shirts with ''31-0 Not Done Yet'' in white. Kentucky became the first team from a [[Power 5 conferences|Power 5]] conference to achieve a perfect record during the regular season in over twenty-five years.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030715aaa.html|title=Kentucky Beats Florida, Completes Undefeated Regular Season|access-date=2015-03-07|date=2015-03-07|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150311063538/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030715aaa.html|archive-date=2015-03-11|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400597432|title=Florida vs Kentucky boxscore|access-date=2015-03-07|date=2015-03-07|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} ===SEC tournament=== Kentucky entered the [[2015 SEC men's basketball tournament|2015 SEC tournament]] as the top-overall seed and bye until the quarterfinals. The SEC tournament took place at [[Bridgestone Arena]] in [[Nashville, Tennessee|Nashville]]. On March 13, Kentucky met Florida for the third time of the season with the right to go to the semifinals of the SEC tournament. In the day prior, Florida defeated Alabama in the second round to advance to the quarterfinals. Aaron Harrison and Towns each scored 13 points and Kentucky shut down Florida in the second half to pull away for a 64–49 victory. The height advantage helped Kentucky outrebound Florida 39 to 33, including a 16 to 11 edge offensively that created extra chances and earned frequent trips to the free-throw line. Towns also had 12 boards.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400784919|title=Florida vs Kentucky SEC boxscore|access-date=2015-03-13|date=2015-03-13|work=[[ESPN.com]]}}{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/031315aab.html|title=Towns, Aaron Harrison Help Kentucky Top Florida in SECT Quarters|access-date=2015-03-13|date=2015-03-13|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150315165526/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/031315aab.html|archive-date=2015-03-15|url-status=dead}} On March 14 Kentucky met Auburn in the semifinals of the SEC tournament. In the day prior, Auburn upset LSU in overtime. Kentucky poured it on against an Auburn squad that lost two players in less than 24 hours. Auburn forward Jordon Granger was suspended for fighting in Friday's quarterfinal win over LSU, and the school announced just before the tipoff that forward Cinmeon Bowers had been suspended for a potential rules violation. Cauley-Stein scored 18 points and Andrew Harrison added 15 to help Kentucky improve to 33–0 in a 91 to 67 victory over the Tigers and advance to the finals of the SEC tournament. The win broke the school-record winning streak of 32 games set from December 5, 1953, to January 8, 1955.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400785062|title=Auburn vs Kentucky SEC boxscore|access-date=2015-03-14|date=2015-03-14|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} On March 15 Kentucky met Arkansas in the title game of the SEC tournament. The Razorbacks defeated Georgia in the semifinals the day prior. Cauley-Stein scored 15 points and grabbed 10 rebounds, and Kentucky never trailed in beating No. 21 Arkansas 78 to 63 for the program's 28th SEC tournament title. Kentucky scored the first eight points as Andrew Harrison hit two 3s early. Arkansas had not trailed in this tournament, yet against Kentucky the best the Razorbacks could do was tie the game four times with the last at 19-all on a 3-pointer by Qualls with 7:59 left. By the time the Razorbacks worked the ball inside against Kentucky's blue wall, they struggled to knock down shots. After Qualls' 3, they didn't score another field goal the rest of the half. The semifinals and finals of the region were held in [[Cleveland, Ohio|Cleveland]]. ====Round of 64==== On [[Selection Sunday]], it was announced that Kentucky would play its opening round games in Louisville at the [[KFC Yum! Center]] against the winner of a play-in game between [[2014–15 Hampton Pirates men's basketball team|Hampton]] and [[2014–15 Manhattan Jaspers basketball team|Manhattan]]. Hampton defeated Manhattan 74–64 on March 17. On March 20, Kentucky played Hampton and defeated the Pirates 79–56. Towns bounced back from a mini slump with 21 points and 11 rebounds, Andrew Harrison added 14 points, and the Wildcats rolled to an opening game victory.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/032015aaa.html|title=Towns' Double-Double Leads Kentucky Past Hampton|access-date=2015-03-20|date=2015-03-20|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150322133351/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/032015aaa.html|archive-date=2015-03-22|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400785343|title=Hampton vs Kentucky NCAA boxscore|access-date=2015-03-20|date=2015-03-20|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} ====Round of 32==== On March 20, 8th-seeded [[2014–15 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati]] and 9th-seeded [[2014–15 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]] squared off in the game prior to Kentucky and Hampton playing. The Bearcats outlasted the Boilermakers 66–65 in overtime. On March 22 Cincinnati and Kentucky met in Louisville for a berth to the Sweet 16. This was the first meeting between the two programs since the [[2005 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2005 NCAA tournament]] in which Kentucky won. The game was not as easy for the Wildcats like it was in the opening round game against Hampton. Kentucky shot just 37 percent and was outrebounded 45 to 38 yet always seemed in control because of timely baskets and rebounds that Cincinnati failed to get. The physical, pesky Bearcats made the Wildcats work hard for every shot and rebound in an intense contest. Yet the Wildcats succeeded by making life difficult on both ends for Cincinnati, holding the Bearcats to 32 percent shooting including just 24 percent in the second half. Kentucky blocked six shots after halftime and nine overall while also coming up with key rebounds. Kentucky outlasted Cincinnati's physicality, defeating the Bearcats 64 to 51 en route to the Sweet 16.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/032115aaa.html|title=Sweet 16: Lyles, Aaron Harrison Lead Kentucky in Win Over Cincinnati|access-date=2015-03-22|date=2015-03-22|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150324141640/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/032115aaa.html|archive-date=2015-03-24|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400786203|title=Cincinnati vs Kentucky NCAA boxscore|access-date=2015-03-22|date=2015-03-22|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} ====Midwest Regional semifinals==== On March 21, 4th-seeded Maryland faced off against 5th-seeded [[2014–15 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team|West Virginia]]. The Mountaineers defeated the Terrapins 69–59 to set up a match-up against Kentucky in the Sweet 16 in Cleveland. Prior to the game on March 26, West Virginia guard Daxter Miles Jr. guaranteed that the Mountaineers would hand the Wildcats their first loss of the season, claiming the Wildcats were going to be 36–1.{{cite web|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2015/03/25/wvus-miles-kentucky-is-gonna-be-36-1/70446880/|title=Daxter Miles guarantee|access-date=2015-03-25|date=2015-03-25|publisher=[[Courier-Journal]]|author=Tucker, Kyle}} The comment by Miles made ESPN's [[SportsCenter]] prior to the game and created a lot of commentary prior to the game about the Mountaineers chances against the Wildcats. The commentary by the West Virginia player only fueled the Kentucky players. Within the first eight minutes, Kentucky built an 18 to 2 lead. Rendering West Virginia's full-court pressure wholly ineffective, UK committed just 10 turnovers for the game and shot a scalding 60.9 percent from the field in building an insurmountable 44–18 lead. The Mountaineers, meanwhile, were flummoxed on offense. They shot 24.1 percent from the field for the game and at one point had made just 5-of-37 attempts. All told, they managed just 0.582 points per possession and their 39 points were a season low. UK, meanwhile, blocked seven shots. Six players combined for UK's 13 assists on 24 made field goals, while more good passes helped lead to the Cats' 31 free-throw attempts, of which they hit 26. Trey Lyles hit 6-of-7 tries from the line in pacing UK with 14 points, while Andrew Harrison scored nine of his 13 points at the line. Kentucky defeated West Virginia 78–39, tying the largest margin of victory ever in a regional semifinal.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/032715aaa.html|title=Walking the walk: Cats cruise past West Virginia, into Elite Eight|access-date=2015-03-27|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150329224016/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/032715aaa.html|archive-date=2015-03-29}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400786514|title=West Virginia vs Kentucky NCAA boxscore|access-date=2015-03-27|date=2015-03-27|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} ====Midwest Regional Finals==== On March 26, 3rd-seeded Notre Dame faced off against [[2014–15 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]] for a berth to the Elite Eight. Notre Dame defeated Wichita State 81 to 70 to set up a meeting with Kentucky two nights later. On March 28 Kentucky and Notre Dame met for a berth to the Final Four. In a game that was considered one of the greatest in NCAA tournament history, Kentucky defeated Notre Dame 68–66. Kentucky needed its players to step up in a big game with such high stakes. Towns was foremost among players stepping up when it mattered most. The 6-foot-11 forward played through foul trouble to score nine of his career-best 25 points over that final stretch, including the game-tying basket in the post with 1:12 left. The big 3 came with 3:15 on the clock. The Cats, in the midst of a rally after previously trailing by six points with 6:14 to go, trailed by just two when Aaron Harrison pulled up from the right wing. With six seconds left in an Elite Eight matchup with Notre Dame, Andrew Harrison drove and drew a foul on Notre Dame's Demetrius Jackson. Following a timeout called by the Fighting Irish, he toed the line in a 66–66 game and sank two free throws to give Kentucky a two-point lead. The margin remained intact as Notre Dame's Jerian Grant missed a contested 3-pointer as time expired. The game between Kentucky and Notre Dame was the highest rated college basketball game on cable of all time.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400787576|title=Notre Dame vs Kentucky NCAA boxscore|access-date=2015-03-28|date=2015-03-28|work=[[ESPN.com]]}}{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/032815aaa.html|title=Andrew Harrison's free throws cap closing rally, send Cats back to Final Four|access-date=2015-03-28|date=2015-03-28|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150331182740/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/032815aaa.html|archive-date=2015-03-31|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2015/03/29/uk-notre-dame-registers-record-tv-rating/70628814/|title=UK-Notre Dame registers record TV rating|access-date=2015-03-28|date=2015-03-28|publisher=[[Courier-Journal]]|author=Lintner, Jonathan}} ====National semifinal==== On March 26, 1-seeded [[2014–15 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] defeated 2-seeded [[2014–15 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] 85–78 for a berth to the Final Four. This set up a re-match between Kentucky and Wisconsin at the Final Four, this time in Indianapolis. On April 4, Kentucky and Wisconsin faced off for a berth to the National Championship game against [[2014–15 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]]. The Wildcats, once trailing by nine points in the first half and eight early in the second, were poised to close out another opponent in the final minutes, this time in the Final Four. With an 8 to 0 run and their defense holding Wisconsin scoreless for more than six minutes, the Cats grabbed a 60–56 lead with less than five minutes remaining. The Badgers reeled off an 8 to 0 run of their own that Sam Dekker started. Next, Nigel Hayes tied the game with a put-back. It was the last of Wisconsin's 12 offensive rebounds and 13 second-chance points.
